Track the all-positive case separately from the unrestricted-sign case. Give an exact valid example or an unrestricted nonexistence proof; otherwise record only explicitly scoped partial results."},"briefing":"Focus on arbitrary distinct nonzero integer anchors a,b with ab+1 a rational square. Sharpen the supplied denominator restriction for a common rational neighbor, particularly at primes where the valuations of a,b, and the reduced denominator meet different boundary cases. The supplied L3 argument is a starting point, not a global obstruction.

Write x=u/v in lowest terms, v>0. For c in {a,b}, let d_c=gcd(|c|,v). Then gcd(cu+v,v)=d_c. If cx+1 is a rational square, its reduced denominator v/d_c and reduced numerator (cu+v)/d_c must be integer squares. This includes the zero-square case, where the reduced numerator is zero. Thus write v=d_a r^2=d_b s^2 and au+v=d_a A^2, bu+v=d_b B^2, with nonnegative integer square roots. Subtraction gives (b-a)u=d_b B^2-d_a A^2. Preserve possible zero numerators and avoid division by quantities that may vanish.

For each prime p, set e=v_p(v), alpha=v_p(a), beta=v_p(b). The exact conditions are that e-min(e,alpha) and e-min(e,beta) are even. If e is at most both alpha and beta, these conditions impose no parity restriction at p. If e exceeds both, they require alpha and beta to have the same parity, with e of that parity. In the mixed boundary case alpha<e<=beta, they require e-alpha even; symmetrically, beta<e<=alpha requires e-beta even. Hence every prime occurring to an odd exponent in v divides gcd(a,b), and coprime anchors force v to be a square. Do not extend that conclusion to noncoprime anchors: the supplied example a=7, b=329, x=360/12943 has a nonsquare reduced denominator. Determine whether these local conditions, together with the simultaneous numerator-square equations, yield any additional global constraint rather than merely restating the known denominator support.

To connect a genuine arithmetic consequence to the sextuple problem, four distinct common neighbors x_i=u_i/v_i must also satisfy all six cross conditions x_i*x_j+1 in Q^2. Retain nonzero-element and distinctness requirements, including cases where a square root is zero. The infinite common-neighbor graph has a K4 exactly when the fixed anchors extend to a sextuple. Any bounded search or finite parameter range establishes only its finite scope; it cannot settle the unbounded-height problem.

Keep signs explicit. Opposite-sign integer anchors in a tuple must be {-1,1}; negating every element preserves pairwise products and reduces same-sign anchors to positive anchors, but does not imply that other elements are positive. Track the all-positive subcase separately. The canonical order-three seed obstruction applies only when two integers lie in that specified seed triple; it does not cover appended-coordinate placements and is not a substitute for this denominator direction. The supplied degenerate extension family rules out only that particular extension mechanism, not all extensions.

The main existence question remains unresolved in the supplied evidence.","uncertainties":["Whether the simultaneous numerator-square and cross-neighbor equations force an obstruction or permit a nondegenerate K4 for any fixed or varying integer anchors is unresolved.","The supplied example shows that the square-denominator conclusion for coprime anchors cannot simply be extended to noncoprime anchors; no stronger global restriction is established here.","The reported search counts, independent implementation agreement, generated graph data, and fingerprint cannot be independently checked from the supplied artifacts.","No exact sextuple witness or all-anchor, unbounded-height nonexistence proof is supplied; both the all-positive and unrestricted-sign cases remain unresolved.","The external citations and literature locators mentioned in the notes have not been verified."],"selected_attempt_ids":[],"selected_review_ids":[],"emphasis_tags":["integer-anchor-sign-cases","denominator-valuation-boundary-cases","simultaneous-numerator-squares","noncoprime-anchor-limitation","common-neighbor-k4","zero-square-and-distinctness","unbounded-height-obligation","finite-search-is-not-proof","external-citations-unverified"],"selected_lemma_ids":[],"artifact_reading_list":["obj_14dcb588f6032424fc394120a948b17eaff5731bc9f941d2cb176fbfb3b8a8a4","obj_182224f37ce49ffa1c36d92813ff7f6ed8570d23a22e4ec0baf362ebb84756c9"],"diversity_constraints":{"avoid_methods":["Treating another bounded-height or bounded-anchor search as a global proof","Repeating only the existing gcd denominator-support lemma without deriving an additional consequence","Assuming the coprime-anchor square-denominator conclusion holds for noncoprime anchors","Using the canonical order-three seed obstruction as though it covered all integer placements"],"preferred_method_family":"boundary_cases","must_differ_from_prior_attempts":true}}}
